title: SRE standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Summary

This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for: defining and owning SLOs and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident-review expectations, operational tooling, and canonical runbooks. The goal is a single sane set of expectations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so product and platform teams can reliably design, ship, and operate services with predictable economics and customer experience.

Scope

- Applies to all production services owned by Redwood (api, runtime, routing, monitoring, billing).
- Includes hosted API surface, internal control plane, and public-facing observability endpoints.
- Private customer-managed deployments should follow the same SLO framework; deviations must be approved and documented with the security/compliance team.

Principles

1) Customer-facing metrics first: SLOs should reflect customer experience (availability and latency for API calls, correctness for model outputs where measurable).
2) Actionable error budgets: define clear thresholds and deterministic escalation actions when budgets are burned.
3) Capacity tied to SLOs: capacity planning must start from required SLOs and expected traffic distribution.
4) Blameless, timely incident reviews with concrete follow-ups and ownership.
5) Automate operational tooling where it measurably reduces toil (dashboards, runbook automations, capacity autoscaling triggers).

SLO taxonomy and examples

We use a small, consistent set of SLO types: Availability (success rate), Latency (percentile), and Quality (model-specific correctness/accuracy where available). Each SLO entry must include owner, target, measurement window, SLA implications (if any), and error budget policy.

Example SLO table (canonical format - teams must fill for their service):

| service | owner | SLO type | target | window | measurement method | burn action |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| api/public-generate | runtime-team | Availability (5xx+timeouts) | 99.95% | 30d | gateway logs (status code + timeout) | Pager at >25% budget burn in 7d |
| runtime/inference-v2 | runtime-team | Latency p99 (inference tail) | <= 250ms | 30d | distributed tracing + Prometheus histogram | Reduce traffic + enable low-latency variant at 50% burn |
| model-catalog/embeddings | models-team | Availability | 99.9% | 30d | request logs | Notify owner + degrade to cached embeddings at 70% burn |

SLO definition requirements (per service)

- Title: short, unique.
- Service owner: on-call rotation and primary owner.
- SLO metric and target: numeric; prefer percentiles for latency.
- Measurement pipeline: Prometheus/TSDB query or log-derived pipeline with a documented query; include example query.
- Error budget: define error budget units and conversion (e.g., 0.05% downtime of 30d == X minutes).
- Burn policy: thresholds (e.g., 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and deterministic actions per threshold.
- Dependencies: list downstream services and their SLOs considered in error budget allocation.

Error budget policy (standard template)

- Define error budget for the rolling window (default 30d). Convert target to budget units and publish a helper calculation.
- Burn-rate monitoring: set alerts on burn rates computed as (observed error fraction / expected error fraction) over short windows (1h, 6h, 24h).
- Standard escalation:
  1) 25% spent in 7d: inform owner, review immediate mitigations (scaling, cache enablement).
  2) 50% spent in 72h: owner must create mitigation ticket and notify SRE on-call; consider routing or model variant fallback.
  3) 75% spent in 24h: SRE lead involved; consider temporary capacity reservation or traffic shifting.
  4) 100% spent: trigger SEV action and executive notification; freeze non-essential rollouts for affected services.

Capacity planning and run-rate forecasting

Capacity planning is driven by SLOs and expected traffic. The planning workflow:

1) Quarterly demand forecast: product + growth team provide expected QPS and 99th percentile session length for each route.
2) SLO-derived sizing: translate QPS and latency SLO into required serving slots (GPU/CPU), batch sizes, and expected utilization. Use standard sizing spreadsheet (link: /confluence/eng-sre/templates/capacity-sizing-template).
3) Safety buffers: target 15% headroom for normal operations, increase to 30% for new model launches or major events.
4) Autoscaling knobs: define min/max nodes, burst pool capacity, and warm pool policies. Document warm-up times for each platform (e.g., GPU cold-start 180s, container startup 15s).
5) Runbook for capacity shortfall: see Runbooks section.

Capacity metrics to track (minimum):

- Allocated capacity units (GPUs, CPU cores), utilization by hour.
- Request QPS and time-of-day heatmaps.
- Batch fill rate and queue lengths.
- KV cache hit ratio and prefix cache effectiveness.
- Pod/container restart and OOM rates.

Reliability initiatives and investment process

- Quarterly reliability planning: SREs and product leads propose reliability projects tied to measurable outcomes (reduced p99 latency, reduced tail error rate, lower budget burn). Each initiative must include: owner, success metric, hypothesis, rollout plan, rollback criteria, and estimated cost.
- Prioritization: use ROI-driven scoring: impact on error budget/SLOs, implementation cost, and operational complexity.
- Examples of initiatives:
  - KV cache pre-warming for high-traffic models (target: reduce p99 by 20% for inference-v2).
  - Circuit-breaker policy library for model fallbacks (target: reduce user-visible errors by 30%).
  - Improved kernel selection heuristics to reduce 50ms per token at p99 for long sequences.

Incident review standards (post-incident process)

- Timeline:
  - Post-incident triage within 24h (short memo, impact summary).
  - Blameless RCA published within 7 days with timeline, root cause(s), contributing factors, and action items.
  - Action items must include owner and target completion date; tracked in a single JIRA project 'SRE-RETRO'.
- RCAs must follow the template:
  - Summary / Impact (customers affected, SLO impact)
  - Timeline (minute-level for first hour, then 5-15 minute granularity)
  - Root cause(s) (technical and organizational)
  - Corrective actions (immediate and long-term)
  - Prevention plan and verification steps
- Severity definitions and comms: tie severity to error budget preservation, financial impact, and customer SLAs. All SEV1/SEV2 incidents require an executive-notification (email+Slack) and a public postmortem summary redacted for customer data if necessary.

Operational tooling standards

- Dashboards: every SLO must have a dashboard showing SLI trend, error budget burn rate, latency percentiles, and top contributing endpoints. Dashboards must be linked from the SLO document.
- Alerts: two classes only - actionable (must page) and informative (ticket). Minimize noisy alerts; target less than 5 actionable alerts per week per on-call.
- Playbook automation: automate common runbook steps (e.g., scale-up, toggle cached-variant, change routing weight) through a controlled runbook-runner API.
- Pager: integrate with standard paging (PagerDuty). On-call rotations must be published in the SLO document and the team roster.

Canonical runbooks (examples)

1) High inference tail latency (pager: HIGH_LATENCY_INFERENCE)

- Symptoms: p99 latency > 250ms AND batch fill rate < 60% AND request queue length > 50.
- Immediate actions (0-10m):
  1) Acknowledge pager and post status to incident channel (#inc-runtime-high-latency).
  2) Check cluster utilization: kubectl top nodes / GPU metrics. If utilization > 90% and queue growing, scale up by +20% from warm pool.
  3) Enable low-latency model variant (runtime toggle); verify reduction in p99 within 5m.
  4) If high tail persists, divert non-critical traffic to burst pool or degrade to cached responses for eligible routes.
- Investigation (10-60m):
  - Check recent deployments and model rollouts; rollback if deployment correlates with onset.
  - Inspect kernel/driver errors and GPU memory pressure.
  - Check KV cache hit ratio and prefix misses.
- Post-incident: run RCA, update SLO burn entries, and schedule reliability initiative if root cause is systemic.

2) Model-serving CrashLoop / Container restarts (pager: SERVICE_CRASHLOOP)

- Symptoms: 5+ restarts in 10 minutes OR pod restart rate > 5% per hour.
- Immediate actions (0-10m):
  1) Acknowledge and escalate to owning dev on-call.
  2) Capture pod logs (kubectl logs --previous) and systemd/kernel logs for OOM/killing reasons.
  3) If recent image push, rollback to previous image.
  4) If OOM, temporarily reduce batch size and increase memory request, then open a PR to fix memory leak.
- Investigation (10-120m):
  - Reproduce failure in staging with traffic replay where possible.
  - Collect heap/core dumps if available and engage runtime/infra teams.
- Post-incident: document fix, add unit/regression test, and review capacity settings to avoid cascading restarts.

Runbook hygiene and ownership

- Every runbook must list: owner, last-reviewed date, pager names, automated steps (if any), and rollback criteria.
- Review cadence: runbooks associated with high-severity pagers must be reviewed at least every 3 months.
- Runbook tests: each team must run a quarterly game-day to exercise at least one high-severity runbook.

Metrics and reporting

- Weekly SRE report: publish a one-page summary with active error budgets, services at >50% burn, incidents in the past week, and status of reliability initiatives.
- Quarterly reliability review: aggregate trends (p99 latency, availability, budget consumption) and decide on initiative funding.

Ownership and escalation matrix

- Primary: service owner (team on-call).
- Secondary: platform SRE rota.
- Tertiary: SRE lead / Director for organizational escalations.
- Exec notify: for 100% error budget burn for >24h or SEV1 incidents.

Related artifacts and templates

- Capacity sizing template: /confluence/eng-sre/templates/capacity-sizing-template
- SLO document template: /confluence/eng-sre/templates/slo-template
- RCA template: /confluence/eng-sre/templates/rca-template
- Runbook registration: /confluence/eng-sre/runbook-index

Appendix: quick calculations

- Converting availability to minutes per 30d: 99.95% -> ~21.6 minutes downtime/month. 99.9% -> ~43.2 minutes/month.
- Error budget helper: (1 - SLO) * window_minutes.

Contact and maintenance

For questions or exceptions to this standard, contact the platform SRE lead or open a doc PR and add reviewers. This page is owned by the SRE standards working group and reviewed quarterly.
